subject: Load test coordination: k6/Locust scripts, SLO targets, and IP allowlist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Brooks <alex@finlytics.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Load test coordination: k6/Locust scripts, SLO targets, and IP allowlist

Thanks again for the call earlier, Alex and Priya — great discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get to a customer-driven load run next week.

Key SLOs you reiterated on the call:
- P95 latency < 250ms for 512-token generation (non-streaming)
- Sustained throughput target: 1800 requests/minute for the primary route
- Max concurrency observed target: 250 simultaneous sessions
- Streaming path: 100 concurrent streaming connections with per-chunk latency < 40ms

What we need from your side to run a customer-led test: 
1) Confirm a 2-hour test window (preferred: Tue 2026-04-14 02:00-04:00 UTC)
2) Provide a list of source IP ranges for allowlisting (we’ll need both load generators and any CI agents)
3) Test accounts (API keys) or signed test tokens — we can create scoped short-lived keys if you prefer
4) Any custom k6 or Locust scripts you want executed (we have templates attached)

Action items (Redwood):
- Rishi: will provide precise endpoint URLs, rate limits, and a streaming example payload
- Dev: will prepare a dedicated test instance with isolation and enable token-level tracing for the run
- Me: coordinate scheduling and finalize the mutual action plan (MAP)

Attachments: finlytics-k6-template.js, locustfile-finlytics.py, test-accounts.csv (stubs)

If the proposed window works, we’ll do a quick pre-check 24 hours prior (connectivity, auth, header expectations). Otherwise propose alternative windows.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 17:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Load test coordination: k6/Locust scripts, SLO targets, and IP allowlist

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our infra/security team: 

- We can do Tue 2026-04-14 02:00-04:00 UTC, that slot works for our east-coast staging cluster.
- IP ranges: we have a small pool of load generators and a corporate CI agent. I’m attaching the CIDR list in this thread.
- On auth: we’d prefer Redwood to issue scoped test API keys. Please limit them to the test namespace and set TTL = 6 hours.
- Streaming: we will include streaming traffic in a dedicated phase (15 min) inside the 2-hour window. We’ll instrument both chunk and session metrics.

Two quick asks for Redwood engineers:
1) Please confirm if the streaming endpoint requires websocket upgrade or if it’s HTTP chunked (our testing tools differ).
2) Can you share a recommended per-worker concurrency for Locust so we don’t accidentally overload a single client VM?

I’m including Priya from ops — she’ll own the allowlist config on our side.

Best,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Finlytics

Attachment: finlytics-ip-pool.txt (CIDRs)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Brooks <alex@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 08:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Load test coordination: k6/Locust scripts, SLO targets, and IP allowlist

Alex — thanks, can confirm technical details: 

Endpoints and protocol
- Non-streaming generation: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate (JSON request body).
- Streaming generation: WebSocket upgrade to wss://stream.redwood.com/v1/stream (we also support chunked HTTP streaming at /v1/stream-http if you prefer not to use websockets).

Auth and test keys
- Marissa: we’ll create scoped API keys for the finlytics-test namespace with 6h TTL. Keys will be IP-locked to your CIDRs if you want that.

Performance knobs and recommended client config
- Recommended per-Locust-worker concurrency: 50 greenlets (safe starting point). Scale worker VMs horizontally instead of cranking per-worker threads.
- k6 script: iterations with ramping VUs; see attached finlytics-k6-template.js. Use checks to validate 200 + token count in body.
- For streaming: we recommend an initial limit of 20 concurrent streaming connections per worker VM to avoid hitting client-side websocket bottlenecks. We can increase if your infra supports it.

Test window and telemetry
- We’ll enable token-level tracing and per-route latency breakdown for the run. Please send the list of metrics you’ll collect and the DataDog/Prometheus endpoints if you want our traces forwarded.

Let us know if we should whitelist the CI agent addresses too; we’ll do the allowlist config the morning of the test.

Thanks,
Rishi
Staff Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: streaming-example-payload.json (sample)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finlytics.com>, Alex Brooks <alex@finlytics.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Load test coordination: k6/Locust scripts, SLO targets, and IP allowlist

Hi all — thanks for the attachments. I’ve done a quick review of the Finlytics Locust file and the k6 template and a few operational notes before the run: 

- I’ll provision a dedicated test mesh isolated from prod traffic and pin a small fleet (3 x n1-gpu-s) to emulate your traffic profile.
- Locust worker guidance: start with 10 workers x 50 greenlets (500 concurrency across workers) and ramp by 10% every 5 minutes until we hit the 250 concurrent sessions target. We’ll watch queue depth on the serving nodes and throttle via our gateway if needed.
- k6: use stages to ramp from 50 to 300 VUs over 20 minutes then hold. The attached finlytics-k6-template.js includes environment variables for your token and endpoint.
- IP allowlist: please send the final CIDRs by 2026-04-13 12:00 UTC. We’ll apply the firewall rules and confirm via a pre-check script (I’ll share a connect-check URL).
- Post-run artifacts: we’ll export raw token-level traces, per-route histograms, and compressed logs (S3 link) within 4 hours of test completion.

I’ll create the scoped API keys once the CIDRs arrive. If you’d like, we can do a 15-minute dry-run 1 hour before the window to validate auth and connectivity.

Cheers,
Dev
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: locustfile-finlytics.py (annotated review)
